subject: Feature lock-in concerns and flexible tiering — clarification and proposed MAP
messages:
From: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@integralhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial questions on tiering flexibility and feature lock-in

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the proposal you sent last week — the team reviewed it and we have a couple of areas we need clarified before moving to procurement. High-level questions:

- What does Redwood consider a \"locked\" feature vs. an \"add-on\" for the purposes of switching tiers? If we start on the Standard tier and later need a specific capability (prefix caching+KV persistence in Private), will that require a migration project?
- Are there any hard dependencies that bind us to a particular model variant or quantization profile if we choose a lower-cost tier later?
- For committed spend discounts, is there a straight proration if we scale up mid-term?

We want to avoid a scenario where we choose a lower-cost plan for Q3 and then can’t restore prior throughput without a long migration. Can you share a short MAP (mutual action plan) and any migration windows that you support?

Appreciate it — Amanda
Purchasing Manager, Integral Health

Attachment: Proposal_v1.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@integralhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on tiering flexibility and feature lock-in

Hi Amanda — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, with detail below and a proposed MAP attached.

1) Feature lock vs add-on: features that are runtime-capability flags (e.g., streaming, function/tool calling) are toggles and can be enabled/disabled across tiers without model migration. Features that require a different runtime configuration (e.g., on-prem KV persistence, specialized quantized kernels) are considered \"compatibility-dependent\" and switching tiers may require a config rollout or a short maintenance window. We do not force a full re-ingest or model conversion for those — typically a rolling restart of dedicated nodes and a config migration (1-4 hours) depending on workload.

2) Model/quantization binding: Redwood exposes model variants and quantization profiles as part of the model catalog. Choosing a lower-cost tier that selects a smaller variant (e.g., 7B quantized) does not destroy your original model artifacts — we preserve the version and can route to it. The catch: restoring previous latency/throughput can require warm-up (KV cache miss penalty) and sometimes a redeploy to larger instance types if you drop below minimum capacity. We document this in the MAP.

3) Proration: committed discounts prorate on a daily basis from the effective change date. If you scale up mid-term, the incremental commit gets its own discount tier for the remainder of the period; full details are in the pricing appendix but yes, proration is standard.

I've attached a concise MAP_v2.pdf that lays out 6 steps (evaluation, pilot, commit, staging migration, live swap, rollback guardrails) and a migration window estimate.

Ben, Kim — adding you for pricing and legal guardrails. Amanda — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk the MAP.

Best,
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_v2.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@integralhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on tiering flexibility and feature lock-in

Amanda — quick note on economics and a small concession to reduce lock-in risk:

- We can add a \"flex escape\" in the contract for the first 9 months: one free tier downgrade/up-swap (no migration fee) to help you test cost savings; after that swaps follow standard migration windows.
- If Integral Health commits to a 12-month minimum (starting at signature) at the proposed Standard+ tier, we'll increase the discount on committed throughput by 5% and provide a one-time migration credit (equivalent to two node-hours on Dedicated) that can be used for a restoration upgrade.

We'd like to preserve the integrity of SLOs, so the escape only applies if the change preserves minimum capacity and operational controls (we'll include thresholds in the MAP).

If that sounds reasonable I can draft language for Kim to fold into the SOW/amendment.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@integralhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on tiering flexibility and feature lock-in

Amanda — legal/ops notes to make this palatable for Procurement: 

- We will add an explicit definition section that separates \"toggle features\" from \"compatibility-dependent features\" so there's no ambiguity.
- The \"flex escape\" will be timeboxed (first 9 months) and limited to one event. We will include an operational checklist that must be followed to qualify (traffic profile snapshot, backup snapshot, scheduled maintenance slot).
- For any Private deployment we will include a rollback playbook and runbook with estimated RTO/RPO; these are part of the onboarding deliverables.

Ben — please send the concession language and I'll prepare a short amendment template we can attach to the SOW. Amanda — happy to review the amendment with your procurement counsel if helpful.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@integralhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Initial questions on tiering flexibility and feature lock-in

Thanks all — this addresses our main concerns. A couple of follow-ups before we route to procurement: 

- Please insert the flex-escape language and the operational checklist into the MAP_v2 and re-share.
- We need the migration-credit details spelled out (how it's redeemed and any expiry).
- Can you confirm the one-hour warm-up assumption for restoring KV cache is a conservative estimate for our expected 6k qps pilot? If not, give a range so we can plan for degraded latency during restoration.

If you can turn around those three edits by EOD Friday we can aim to open a PO next week and sign the SOW amendment the same day.

Best,
Amanda
Purchasing Manager, Integral Health
